successCriteria: A 14-day April Japan itinerary covering Tokyo, Kyoto, and a few days of hiking is fully booked (flights, lodging, intercity transport, hike logistics), total cost lands at or under ~$4,000, and all travel-document, gear, and reservation logistics are confirmed before departure.
rationale: April in Japan is peak cherry-blossom season, so the binding constraint is availability and price, not itinerary design. Structuring the plan as budget-first, then book-transport and book-lodging in parallel, then itinerary against what's actually secured prevents building a plan that must later be unwound. The hiking leg is deliberately placed as a separate booking task because trail-accessible lodging and seasonal trail openings (many alpine routes are closed or snowbound in early April) are the most likely thing to break the $4,000 budget or the schedule.

tasks.description: Research April Japan trip specifics: cherry-blossom timing by city, Golden Week dates to avoid, which hiking areas are actually open/trail-accessible in April, and current entry/document requirements.
Build a line-item budget against the ~$4,000 cap (flights, intercity transport/JR Pass, lodging, food, hiking costs) and set per-category ceilings that the bookings must respect.
Book round-trip international flights and intercity transport (e.g. Tokyo–Kyoto rail / JR Pass decision), targeting April dates outside Golden Week.
Book lodging for Tokyo, Kyoto, and the hiking base(s), respecting budget ceilings and April availability.
Build the day-by-day 14-day itinerary sequencing Tokyo, the hiking days, and Kyoto around the confirmed transport and lodging.
Handle travel logistics: IC transit card, eSIM/connectivity, travel insurance, passport validity check, and any hike reservations or gear arrangements.
Final pre-departure check: itinerary and reservations confirmed, weather/trail conditions reviewed, documents and packing verified against the forecast.
